title: Start Again
subtitle: A New Year journey in 5 stops

stops.title: New Every Morning
stops.summary: In the ruins of Jerusalem, the writer remembers one thing that hasn't been destroyed: God's mercy.
stops.why: Lamentations is written from the worst moment in Israel's history. Right in the middle of the grief is this: His compassions fail not, they are new every morning. You don't need a new year to start over. You get a new morning.

quiz.q: What does the writer say is new every morning?
What does the passage say is good to do?
options: Hope and quietly wait for the LORD

stops.title: Forgetting What's Behind
stops.summary: Paul admits he hasn't arrived, so he forgets what's behind and presses toward the goal.
stops.why: Paul had a past worth forgetting (he hunted Christians) and a résumé worth bragging about. He let go of both. Your worst failures and your best wins can both keep you stuck looking backward.

quiz.q: What does Paul say he forgets?
Does Paul claim he has already arrived?
options: No, he hasn't attained it yet

stops.title: A New Heart
stops.summary: God promises to take out the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh and His own Spirit.
stops.why: Resolutions try to change behavior from the outside. God promises to change you from the inside, a new heart and His Spirit in you. This is a promise to people in exile who had blown it. Real change is something He does in you.

quiz.q: What kind of heart does God take away?
What does He give in its place?
What does God promise to put within His people?

stops.title: Be Strong and Courageous
stops.summary: Moses is dead, and Joshua has to lead a nation into the unknown. God tells him three times to be strong.
stops.why: Joshua had big shoes to fill and a hard road ahead. God didn't promise it would be easy. He promised to be there: "the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest." That's how you walk into a new year.

card.name: Joshua
card.title: The Successor
card.strength: Led Israel into the Promised Land after Moses.
card.weakness: Made a treaty with the Gibeonites without asking God.

quiz.q: Who had just died when this chapter begins?
What did God tell Joshua to do with the book of the law?
options: Meditate on it day and night

quiz.q: "Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid."

stops.title: All Things New
stops.summary: Anyone in Christ is a new creation. The old is gone, and the new has come.
stops.why: This is the deepest fresh start there is. It isn't a better version of the old you; it's a new creation. Then Paul gives you a job: ambassador. A new start comes with a mission.

quiz.q: What does Paul call believers in this passage?
Finish it: "old things are passed away; behold, all things are become ___."
